records.source: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הַמַּלְאָכִ֤ים סְדֹ֨מָה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְל֖וֹט יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר־סְדֹ֑ם וַיַּרְא־לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קָם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And came the two angels to Sodom in the evening, and Lot [was] sitting in [the] gate of Sodom; and saw Lot and rose to meet them and bowed down [with his] face to [the] ground.
pieces: It was evening when the two angels reached Sodom. Lot was sitting at the city gate, and as soon as he saw them he stood up to greet them and bowed low, his face to the ground.

L.1: And the two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot [was] sitting in the gate of Sodom. And Lot saw [them] and rose to meet them, and he bowed down [with his] face to the ground.

R.1: The two angels came to Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the gate of the city. When he saw them, he got up to meet them. He bowed down with his face to the ground.

decisions.choice: the two angels: the two "men" who left Abraham
decisions.reason: The word (mal'akh) means messenger. They are the two of the three visitors who went on toward Sodom (18:22); the story calls them both "angels" (verses 1, 15) and "men" (verses 5, 10, 12, 16).

decisions.choice: sitting in the gate: where the city's business was done
decisions.reason: The gate of a walled town was its public square, where elders met, trade was done and cases were judged (23:10; Ruth 4:1). Lot sitting there suggests he had become a man of standing in Sodom; the men of the city still call him an outsider (verse 9).

records.source: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא־אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל־בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣םלְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין׃
records.gloss: And he said, here, please, my lords, turn aside, please, to [the] house of your servant and stay the night and wash your feet; and you will rise early and go on your way. And they said, no, for in the square we will stay the night.
pieces: "Please, my lords," he said, "come aside to your servant's house. Wash your feet and stay the night, and you can be up early and on your way." "No," they answered, "we will stay out in the square tonight."

L.2: And he said, "Look, my lords, please turn aside to your servant's house and spend the night, and wash your feet. Then you can rise early and go on your way." And they said, "No, we will spend the night in the square."

R.2: He said, "Sirs, please come to my house. You can wash your feet and spend the night there. Then you can get up early and go on your way." But they said, "No, we will spend the night outside in the town square."

decisions.choice: my lords: a polite address to strangers
decisions.reason: Lot does not know they are angels. Like Abraham (18:3-5) he greets travelers with courtesy and offers a place to wash and sleep.

decisions.choice: we will spend the night in the square: refusing at first
decisions.reason: A first refusal was often part of courtesy. The open square near the gate was where a traveler with no host would sleep (Judges 19:15). The refusal also lets the story show what Sodom does to strangers in the open.

records.source: וַיִּפְצַר־בָּ֣ם מְאֹ֔ד וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ אֵלָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וּמַצּ֥וֹת אָפָ֖ה וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And he urged them strongly, and they turned aside to him and came into his house; and he made for them a feast, and unleavened bread he baked, and they ate.
pieces: But he kept pressing them until they turned aside with him and went into his house. He prepared a meal for them and baked bread without yeast, and they ate.

L.3: And he pressed them strongly, and they turned aside to him and came into his house. And he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

R.3: But Lot kept begging them, so they went with him into his house. He made a big meal for them and baked flat bread without yeast, and they ate.

decisions.choice: a feast: a meal with drink
decisions.reason: The word (mishteh) comes from the verb "to drink" and means a banquet or a meal for guests.

decisions.choice: unleavened bread: bread made quickly, without yeast
decisions.reason: Flat bread without yeast could be baked at once, without waiting for dough to rise. It is the bread of haste, as at the Passover (Exodus 12:39).

records.source: טֶרֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּבוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל־הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד־זָקֵ֑ן כָּל־הָעָ֖ם מִקָּצֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Before they lay down, and [the] men of the city, [the] men of Sodom, surrounded the house, from young [man] and to old, all the people from [every] end.
pieces: They had not yet gone to bed when the men of the city, the men of Sodom, closed in around the house. Young and old, every man from every part of town was there.

L.4: Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, from young to old, all the people from every quarter.

R.4: Before they went to bed, the men of Sodom came and surrounded Lot's house. Young men and old men came from every part of the city.

decisions.choice: from young to old, all the people from every quarter: the whole city
decisions.reason: The words stress that the whole male population took part, not a few. Abraham had asked whether ten righteous people could be found there (18:32); the scene shows the answer.

records.source: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֶל־לוֹט֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ אַיֵּ֧ה הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַלָּ֑יְלָה הוֹצִיאֵ֣ם אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְנֵדְעָ֖ה אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they called to Lot and said to him, where [are] the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them.
pieces: They shouted to Lot, "Where are the men who came to stay with you tonight? Send them out to us. We mean to have sex with them."

L.5: And they called to Lot and said to him, "Where [are] the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them."

R.5: They shouted to Lot, "Where are the men who came to your house tonight? Send them out to us. We want to have sex with them."

decisions.choice: that we may know them: that we may have sex with them
alternatives: that we may get to know who they are
decisions.reason: "Know" (yada) is used for sexual relations (4:1), and Lot's answer in verse 8, offering daughters "who have not known a man", shows that this is the sense. The crowd intends to rape the guests by force. Their sin is both sexual violence and a violent breach of the duty to protect strangers (Judges 19:22; Ezekiel 16:49; Jude 7).

decisions.choice: have sex with them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the meaning plainly; Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "know".

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֧א אֲלֵהֶ֛ם ל֖וֹט הַפֶּ֑תְחָה וְהַדֶּ֖לֶת סָגַ֥ר אַחֲרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And went out to them Lot to the entrance, and the door he shut behind him.
pieces: Lot went out to them at the doorway and closed the door behind him.

L.6: And Lot went out to them at the entrance, and shut the door behind him,

R.6: Lot went outside to talk to them, and he shut the door behind him.

decisions.choice: shut the door behind him: protecting his guests
decisions.reason: Lot puts himself between the crowd and his guests. A host was bound to protect those who had come under his roof (verse 8).

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אַל־נָ֥א אַחַ֖י תָּרֵֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said, do not, please, my brothers, do evil.
pieces: "My friends," he said, "please do not commit this wicked act.

L.7: and he said, "Please, my brothers, do not do [this] evil.

R.7: He said, "My friends, please do not do such an evil thing.

decisions.choice: my brothers: fellow townsmen
decisions.reason: Lot appeals to the crowd as neighbors. They reject the claim: to them he is still a foreigner (verse 9).

decisions.choice: my friends
decisions.reason: The men are not Lot's relatives; "brothers" here is a friendly appeal to neighbors, which "friends" conveys. Literal keeps "brothers".

records.source: הִנֵּה־נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אוֹצִֽיאָה־נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל־תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Here, please, to me [are] two daughters who have not known a man; let me bring them out, please, to you, and do to them as [is] good in your eyes; only to these men do not do anything, for therefore they have come under [the] shadow of my roof.
pieces: Listen, I have two daughters who have never been with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do with them whatever you please. But do nothing to these men, because they have come under the protection of my roof."

L.8: Look, I have two daughters who have not known a man. Let me bring them out to you, and do to them as [is] good in your eyes. Only do nothing to these men, for that is why they have come under the shadow of my roof."

R.8: Look, I have two daughters who are virgins. Let me bring them out to you. You can do whatever you want with them. But do not do anything to these men. They are guests in my house, and I must protect them."

decisions.choice: Lot offers his daughters: a terrible offer, reported without approval
decisions.reason: Lot is willing to hand his own daughters to the mob to protect his guests. The narrator reports the offer without comment, but the story that follows (verses 30-38) shows the damage done to this family. The same horror is repeated in Judges 19:24.

decisions.choice: under the shadow of my roof: under my protection as host
decisions.reason: Guests who had entered a man's house were under his protection; to harm them was to dishonor him.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ׀גֶּשׁ־הָ֗לְאָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ הָאֶחָ֤ד בָּֽא־לָגוּר֙ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֣ט שָׁפ֔וֹט עַתָּ֕ה נָרַ֥ע לְךָ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם וַיִּפְצְר֨וּ בָאִ֤ישׁ בְּלוֹט֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֖וּ לִשְׁבֹּ֥ר הַדָּֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: And they said, step away beyond. And they said, the one came to sojourn and he keeps judging; now we will do harm to you more than to them. And they pressed against the man, against Lot, strongly, and came near to break the door.
pieces: "Get out of the way!" they shouted. "This fellow came here as a foreigner, and now he wants to play the judge! We will do worse to you than to them." They pushed hard against Lot and moved in to break down the door.

L.9: But they said, "Step back!" And they said, "This one came to live [here] as a foreigner, and he keeps acting as judge! Now we will treat you worse than them." And they pressed hard against the man, against Lot, and came near to break the door.

R.9: "Get out of our way!" they said. "You came here as a stranger, and now you want to tell us what is right! We will do worse things to you than to them!" They pushed hard against Lot and tried to break down the door.

decisions.choice: came to live as a foreigner ... acting as judge: an outsider presuming to judge
decisions.reason: "Sojourn" (gur) is to live in a place as a resident foreigner. The doubled verb "judging, he judges" mocks Lot for passing judgment on the city's citizens. The word for judging recalls Abraham's plea to the Judge of all the earth (18:25).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת־יָדָ֔ם וַיָּבִ֧יאוּ אֶת־ל֛וֹט אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְאֶת־הַדֶּ֖לֶת סָגָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And stretched out the men their hand and brought Lot to them into the house, and the door they shut.
pieces: But the two men inside reached out, pulled Lot back into the house with them and shut the door.

L.10: But the men put out their hand and brought Lot into the house with them, and they shut the door.

R.10: But the two men inside reached out and pulled Lot back into the house. Then they shut the door.

decisions.choice: the two men inside
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls both the guests and the crowd "the men". Balanced and Readable say "the two men inside" so that the reader knows the angels are meant.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים אֲשֶׁר־פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּ֗יִת הִכּוּ֙ בַּסַּנְוֵרִ֔ים מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד־גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּלְא֖וּ לִמְצֹ֥א הַפָּֽתַח׃
records.gloss: And the men who [were at the] entrance of the house they struck with blindness, from small and to great, and they wore themselves out to find the entrance.
pieces: Then they struck the men at the doorway with a blinding light, every one of them, young and old, so that they groped about in vain for the door.

L.11: And they struck the men who [were at] the entrance of the house with blindness, from small to great, so that they wore themselves out trying to find the entrance.

R.11: Then the angels made the men at the door unable to see, both young and old. The men could not find the door, and they finally gave up.

decisions.choice: blindness: a sudden dazzling or confusion
decisions.reason: The word (sanwerim) occurs only here and in 2 Kings 6:18, where an army is struck so that it cannot recognize where it is. It seems to be a sudden blinding or bewildering rather than ordinary blindness.

decisions.choice: a blinding light
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "a blinding light" to suggest a sudden dazzling rather than lasting blindness; Literal keeps "blindness", and Readable says they could not see.

decisions.choice: the angels
decisions.reason: Readable names the angels as the ones who acted.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֶל־ל֗וֹט עֹ֚ד מִֽי־לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה חָתָן֙ וּבָנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־לְךָ֖ בָּעִ֑יר הוֹצֵ֖א מִן־הַמָּקֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And said the men to Lot, yet who [is] to you here? Son-in-law and your sons and your daughters and all who [are] to you in the city, bring out from the place.
pieces: Then the men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of this place,

L.12: And the men said to Lot, "Who else [do] you [have] here? A son-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and anyone you [have] in the city, bring [them] out of this place.

R.12: Then the two men said to Lot, "Do you have any other family in this city? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone else? Get them out of here,

decisions.choice: a son-in-law: listed first
decisions.reason: The son-in-law is named first, perhaps because Lot's daughters were promised in marriage (verse 14). Sons are mentioned, but none appear in the story.

records.source: כִּֽי־מַשְׁחִתִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ אֶת־הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־גָֽדְלָ֤ה צַעֲקָתָם֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For about to destroy [are] we this place, for great [is] their outcry before YHWH, and has sent us YHWH to destroy it.
pieces: because we are going to destroy it. The outcry against its people has grown so great before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent us to destroy the city."

L.13: for we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has become great before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent us to destroy it."

R.13: because we are going to destroy this city. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has heard the terrible cries against its people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent us to destroy it."

decisions.choice: their outcry: the cry of 18:20-21
decisions.reason: The angels take up the word of 18:20-21. The LORD has come down and seen, and the outcry was true.

decisions.choice: destroy: ruin completely
decisions.reason: The verb (shachat) is the one used for the flood (6:13, 17). The city has become as corrupt as the world before the flood (6:11-12).

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֨א ל֜וֹט וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר׀אֶל־חֲתָנָ֣יו׀לֹקְחֵ֣י בְנֹתָ֗יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙ מִן־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־מַשְׁחִ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הָעִ֑יר וַיְהִ֥י כִמְצַחֵ֖ק בְּעֵינֵ֥י חֲתָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And went out Lot and spoke to his sons-in-law, [who were] taking his daughters, and said, arise, go out from this place, for about to destroy [is] YHWH the city. And he was like one jesting in [the] eyes of his sons-in-law.
pieces: So Lot went out and told the men who were engaged to his daughters, "Hurry, leave this place! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is going to destroy the city!" But his sons-in-law thought he was not serious.

L.14: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were to marry his daughters, and said, "Get up, get out of this place, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to destroy the city." But in the eyes of his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.

R.14: So Lot went out and talked to the men who were going to marry his daughters. He said, "Hurry and get out of this place! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is about to destroy the city!" But they thought he was joking.

decisions.choice: who were to marry his daughters: engaged, or already married
alternatives: who had married his daughters (other daughters, left behind)
decisions.reason: The participle "taking" can mean "who were about to take" or "who had taken". Since the two daughters at home have "not known a man" (verse 8), the likely sense is that they were engaged. Some have read it as other, married daughters who died in the city.

decisions.choice: joking: the root of Isaac's name
decisions.reason: The verb (tsachaq) is the one for laughing in 17:17 and 18:12-15, which gives Isaac his name (21:6). Here it means to jest: the sons-in-law did not take the warning seriously.

records.source: וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת־אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן־תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And as the dawn came up, and urged the angels Lot, saying, arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are found [here], lest you be swept away in the punishment of the city.
pieces: As day was breaking, the angels pressed Lot to hurry. "Up!" they said. "Take your wife and the two daughters who are here with you, or you will be swept away when the city is punished."

L.15: And as the dawn came up, the angels urged Lot, saying, "Get up, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city."

R.15: At dawn the angels told Lot to hurry. "Get up!" they said. "Take your wife and your two daughters who are here. Go, or you will die when the city is punished."

decisions.choice: punishment: guilt and its penalty
decisions.reason: The word (avon) means both wrongdoing and the punishment it brings (4:13). Here it is the city's sin coming back upon it.

decisions.choice: swept away: the word of Abraham's plea
decisions.reason: The verb (saphah) is the one Abraham used: "Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?" (18:23). The angels make sure that does not happen to Lot.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְמַהְמָ֓הּ׀וַיַּחֲזִ֨קוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּיָד֣וֹ וּבְיַד־אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּבְיַד֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתָ֔יו בְּחֶמְלַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיֹּצִאֻ֥הוּ וַיַּנִּחֻ֖הוּ מִח֥וּץ לָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And he lingered; and seized the men his hand and [the] hand of his wife and [the] hand of his two daughters, in [the] mercy of YHWH upon him, and brought him out and set him outside the city.
pieces: When he still hesitated, the men took hold of his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had pity on him. They led him out and left him outside the city.

L.16: But he lingered. So the men seized his hand and the hand of his wife and the hands of his two daughters, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was merciful to him, and they brought him out and set him outside the city.

R.16: But Lot was slow to leave. So the two men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and two daughters, and they led them out of the city. They did this because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had mercy on Lot.

decisions.choice: he lingered: he hesitated
decisions.reason: The verb (hitmahmah) means to delay or hesitate. Even with destruction at hand, Lot is slow to leave what he has in Sodom.

decisions.choice: because the LORD was merciful to him: rescue as an act of mercy
decisions.reason: Lot is saved not because he is quick or deserving but because of the LORD's compassion (chemlah), and because God remembered Abraham (verse 29).

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כְהוֹצִיאָ֨ם אֹתָ֜ם הַח֗וּצָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הִמָּלֵ֣ט עַל־נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ אַל־תַּבִּ֣יט אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ וְאַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֖ד בְּכָל־הַכִּכָּ֑ר הָהָ֥רָה הִמָּלֵ֖ט פֶּן־תִּסָּפֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was, as they brought them outside, and he said, escape for your life; do not look behind you, and do not stop in all the valley; to the hill country escape, lest you be swept away.
pieces: Once they had brought them out, one of them said, "Run for your lives! Do not look behind you or stop anywhere on the plain. Flee to the hills, or you will be swept away!"

L.17: And as they brought them outside, one said, "Escape for your life! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere in the valley. Escape to the hills, or you will be swept away."

R.17: When they were outside the city, one of the angels said, "Run for your lives! Do not look back. Do not stop anywhere in the valley. Run to the hills, or you will die!"

decisions.choice: he said: one of the two speaks
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. From here to verse 22 one of the angels speaks, and in verses 21-22 he speaks with the LORD's authority to spare a city.

decisions.choice: the valley: the plain of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The word (kikkar) is the round plain of the Jordan that Lot chose for its water (13:10-12).

decisions.choice: one said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said" after a plural subject; "one" makes clear that one of the angels speaks.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹט אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אַל־נָ֖א אֲדֹנָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Lot to them, no, please, my lord.
pieces: But Lot said to them, "Please, my lord, not that!

L.18: And Lot said to them, "Oh no, my lord, please!

R.18: But Lot said to them, "No, sir, please!

decisions.choice: my lord: Lot addresses the angel; the Masoretic vowels read "Lord"
decisions.reason: The word can be "my lords", "my lord" or the title used for God (Adonai). The Masoretic vowels give the form used for God, and in verse 21 the angel grants the request with God's authority. Lot speaks to one of the two ("your servant", "your eyes" are singular in verse 19), and the translation treats him as addressing the angel, as in 18:3.

records.source: הִנֵּה־נָ֠א מָצָ֨א עַבְדְּךָ֣ חֵן֮ בְּעֵינֶיךָ֒ וַתַּגְדֵּ֣ל חַסְדְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ עִמָּדִ֔י לְהַחֲי֖וֹת אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֑י וְאָנֹכִ֗י לֹ֤א אוּכַל֙ לְהִמָּלֵ֣ט הָהָ֔רָה פֶּן־תִּדְבָּקַ֥נִי הָרָעָ֖ה וָמַֽתִּי׃
records.gloss: Here, please, has found your servant favor in your eyes, and you have made great your loyalty which you have done with me to keep alive my life; and I am not able to escape to the hill country, lest cling to me the disaster and I die.
pieces: You have been kind to your servant and have shown me great mercy by saving my life. But I cannot get as far as the hills. The disaster will catch me before I get there, and I will die.

L.19: Look, your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have shown great loyalty to me in saving my life. But I cannot escape to the hills, or the disaster will overtake me and I will die.

R.19: You have been very kind to me and have saved my life. But I cannot run all the way to the hills. The disaster will catch up with me, and I will die.

decisions.choice: loyalty: steadfast kindness
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is faithful, generous kindness, the love that keeps faith with someone (24:12; 32:10).

decisions.choice: the disaster will cling to me: it will overtake me
decisions.reason: The verb (davaq) means to stick to or catch up with (31:23). Lot fears the destruction will reach him on the way.

records.source: הִנֵּה־נָ֠א הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֧את קְרֹבָ֛ה לָנ֥וּס שָׁ֖מָּה וְהִ֣יא מִצְעָ֑ר אִמָּלְטָ֨ה נָּ֜א שָׁ֗מָּה הֲלֹ֥א מִצְעָ֛ר הִ֖וא וּתְחִ֥י נַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: Here, please, the city this [is] near to flee there, and it [is] small; let me escape, please, there; [is] it not small? And may live my soul.
pieces: There is a town close by that I can reach, and it is only a small one. Please let me flee there. It is so small, is it not? Then I will live."

L.20: Look, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is a small one. Please let me escape there. Is it not small? Then my life will be spared."

R.20: There is a town near here. It is only a small town. Please let me go there. It is so small! Then I will be safe."

decisions.choice: small: a play on the name Zoar
decisions.reason: "A small thing" (mits'ar) sounds like the town's name, Zoar (verse 22). Lot pleads that so small a place might be spared.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּה֙ נָשָׂ֣אתִי פָנֶ֔יךָ גַּ֖ם לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֛י הָפְכִּ֥י אֶת־הָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, here, I lift up your face also for this matter, not to overthrow the city about which you have spoken.
pieces: "Very well," he answered. "I will grant this request as well. I will not destroy the town you speak of.

L.21: And he said to him, "Look, I grant you this request too: I will not overthrow the city you have spoken of.

R.21: The angel said, "All right. I will do this for you. I will not destroy that town.

decisions.choice: I lift up your face: I grant your request
decisions.reason: To "lift the face" of someone bowed down before you is to receive him with favor and grant what he asks (32:21; 1 Samuel 25:35).

decisions.choice: overthrow: the word used for Sodom's destruction
decisions.reason: The verb (haphakh), "overturn", becomes the standing word for Sodom's fate (verses 25, 29; Deuteronomy 29:23; Amos 4:11).

records.source: מַהֵר֙ הִמָּלֵ֣ט שָׁ֔מָּה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אוּכַל֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת דָּבָ֔ר עַד־בֹּאֲךָ֖ שָׁ֑מָּה עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרָ֥א שֵׁם־הָעִ֖יר צֽוֹעַר׃
records.gloss: Hurry, escape there, for I am not able to do anything until you come there. Therefore one called [the] name of the city Zoar.
pieces: But hurry and get there, because I can do nothing until you arrive." That is why the town came to be called Zoar.

L.22: Hurry, escape there, for I cannot do anything until you arrive there." Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.

R.22: But hurry and get there! I cannot do anything until you are there." That is why the town is called Zoar, which means "small".

decisions.choice: Zoar: "small"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the word for "small" in Lot's plea (verse 20). The town was earlier called Bela (14:2, 8).

decisions.choice: I cannot do anything until you arrive: judgment waits for the righteous to be safe
decisions.reason: The destruction is held back until Lot is safe, an answer to Abraham's plea that the righteous not be swept away with the wicked (18:23-25).

decisions.choice: which means "small"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name.

records.source: הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ יָצָ֣א עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְל֖וֹט בָּ֥א צֹֽעֲרָה׃
records.gloss: The sun had come out over the earth, and Lot came to Zoar.
pieces: By the time Lot reached Zoar, the sun was up over the land.

L.23: The sun had risen over the land when Lot came to Zoar.

R.23: The sun had come up when Lot arrived in Zoar.

decisions.choice: the sun had risen: the time of the disaster
decisions.reason: The angels urged Lot on at dawn (verse 15); the destruction falls in the full light of morning, as soon as he is safe.

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֗ה הִמְטִ֧יר עַל־סְדֹ֛ם וְעַל־עֲמֹרָ֖ה גָּפְרִ֣ית וָאֵ֑שׁ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה מִן־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And YHWH rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from YHWH from the heavens.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent burning sulfur pouring down on Sodom and Gomorrah. It came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, out of the sky.

L.24: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} out of the heavens.

R.24: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made burning sulfur fall like rain on Sodom and Gomorrah. It came down from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the sky.

decisions.choice: sulfur and fire: burning sulfur
decisions.reason: Sulfur (gophrit) burns with choking fumes. The region around the Dead Sea has deposits of sulfur, salt and bitumen (14:10). "Sulfur and fire" became a standard picture of God's judgment (Psalm 11:6; Ezekiel 38:22; Luke 17:29).

decisions.choice: from the LORD out of the heavens: the LORD named twice
decisions.reason: The name is repeated: the LORD rains fire from the LORD. Most simply this stresses that the destruction came from God himself, from heaven, not from a natural accident. Some Christian readers have seen in it a hint of more than one person in God.

records.source: וַֽיַּהֲפֹךְ֙ אֶת־הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הַכִּכָּ֑ר וְאֵת֙ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הֶעָרִ֔ים וְצֶ֖מַח הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he overthrew these cities and all the valley and all [the] inhabitants of the cities and [the] growth of the ground.
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrew those cities and the whole plain, along with everyone who lived in the cities and every plant that grew there.

L.25: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrew those cities, and all the valley, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and what grew on the ground.

R.25: God destroyed those cities and the whole valley. Everyone who lived in the cities died, and all the plants were destroyed.

decisions.choice: overthrew: turned upside down
decisions.reason: The verb (haphakh) means to overturn. The fertile plain that once looked like "the garden of the LORD" (13:10) becomes a wasteland (Deuteronomy 29:23).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the subject at the start of the sentence.

records.source: וַתַּבֵּ֥ט אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מֵאַחֲרָ֑יו וַתְּהִ֖י נְצִ֥יב מֶֽלַח׃
records.gloss: And looked his wife from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
pieces: But Lot's wife, who was following behind him, looked back and was turned into a pillar of salt.

L.26: But his wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.

R.26: But Lot's wife was walking behind him, and she looked back. She became a pillar of salt.

decisions.choice: looked back: disobeying the warning
decisions.reason: The angels had said "Do not look back" (verse 17). Her look back suggests a heart still tied to the city. Jesus says, "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:32).

decisions.choice: a pillar of salt: the salt of the Dead Sea region
decisions.reason: The area around the Dead Sea is full of salt formations. She was caught in the destruction and left as a lasting sign of it.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ם אַבְרָהָ֖ם בַּבֹּ֑קֶר אֶל־הַ֨מָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥מַד שָׁ֖ם אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And rose early Abraham in the morning to the place where he had stood there before YHWH,
pieces: Early the next morning Abraham went back to the place where he had stood in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.27: And Abraham rose early in the morning [and went] to the place where he had stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.27: Early the next morning Abraham went back to the place where he had stood and talked with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the place where he had stood before the LORD: where he had pleaded for Sodom
decisions.reason: Abraham returns to the spot where he had pleaded for the city (18:22-33), to see what had become of it.

decisions.choice: [and went]
decisions.reason: Hebrew lets "to the place" follow "rose early" without a verb of motion; Literal supplies it in brackets.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף עַל־פְּנֵ֤י סְדֹם֙ וַעֲמֹרָ֔ה וְעַֽל־כָּל־פְּנֵ֖י אֶ֣רֶץ הַכִּכָּ֑ר וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה עָלָה֙ קִיטֹ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ כְּקִיטֹ֖ר הַכִּבְשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: and he looked down on [the] face of Sodom and Gomorrah and on all [the] face of [the] land of the valley, and he saw, and there, went up [the] smoke of the land like [the] smoke of the kiln.
pieces: He looked down over Sodom and Gomorrah and across the whole land of the plain, and saw smoke rising from the ground like smoke from a furnace.

L.28: and he looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the valley, and he saw, and look, the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a kiln.

R.28: He looked down at Sodom and Gomorrah and the whole valley. He saw thick smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a huge oven.

decisions.choice: kiln: a furnace for firing pottery or lime
decisions.reason: The word (kivshan) is a large furnace. The same picture describes Mount Sinai wrapped in smoke (Exodus 19:18).

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּשַׁחֵ֤ת אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־עָרֵ֣י הַכִּכָּ֔ר וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיְשַׁלַּ֤ח אֶת־לוֹט֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָ֔ה בַּהֲפֹךְ֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יָשַׁ֥ב בָּהֵ֖ן לֽוֹט׃
records.gloss: And it was, when destroyed God the cities of the valley, and remembered God Abraham and sent out Lot from [the] midst of the overthrow when he overthrew the cities in which had lived Lot.
pieces: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the disaster that overturned the cities where Lot had made his home.

L.29: So it was that when God destroyed the cities of the valley, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrew the cities in which Lot had lived.

R.29: When God destroyed the cities in the valley, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered Abraham. So God brought Lot safely out of the cities where he had lived before he destroyed them.

decisions.choice: God remembered Abraham: Lot is saved for Abraham's sake
decisions.reason: "Remember" means to act on someone's behalf (8:1). The summary explains that Lot was rescued because of Abraham's plea (18:23-32), not because of Lot's own merit.

records.source: וַיַּעַל֩ ל֨וֹט מִצּ֜וֹעַר וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בָּהָ֗ר וּשְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י יָרֵ֖א לָשֶׁ֣בֶת בְּצ֑וֹעַר וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה ה֖וּא וּשְׁתֵּ֥י בְנֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And went up Lot from Zoar and lived in the hill country, and his two daughters with him, for he was afraid to live in Zoar; and he lived in the cave, he and his two daughters.
pieces: Afterward Lot left Zoar and settled in the hills with his two daughters, because he was afraid to stay in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.

L.30: And Lot went up from Zoar and lived in the hills, and his two daughters with him, for he was afraid to live in Zoar. And he lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.

R.30: Later Lot was afraid to stay in Zoar. So he and his two daughters left and went to live in the hills. They lived in a cave.

decisions.choice: afraid to live in Zoar: Lot ends where the angel first sent him
decisions.reason: Lot had begged to go to Zoar rather than the hills (verses 19-20); now fear drives him to the hills after all. The man who once chose the best land (13:10-11) ends up living in a cave.

records.source: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר הַבְּכִירָ֛ה אֶל־הַצְּעִירָ֖ה אָבִ֣ינוּ זָקֵ֑ן וְאִ֨ישׁ אֵ֤ין בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ לָב֣וֹא עָלֵ֔ינוּ כְּדֶ֖רֶךְ כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And said the firstborn to the younger, our father [is] old, and a man there is not in the land to come in to us according to [the] way of all the earth.
pieces: One day the older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is getting old, and there is no man anywhere around to marry us and give us children, as is the custom everywhere.

L.31: And the firstborn said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is not a man in the land to come in to us after the way of all the earth.

R.31: One day the older daughter said to her younger sister, "Our father is old. There is no man around here who can marry us and give us children, as men do everywhere.

decisions.choice: there is not a man in the land: no husband for them
decisions.reason: They may have thought the whole region destroyed, or simply that no man would marry the daughters of a refugee living in a cave. Either way, they see no future for the family line.

decisions.choice: to come in to us after the way of all the earth: to marry us and father children
decisions.reason: "Come in to" is the usual idiom for marriage and sexual relations (16:2); "the way of all the earth" means the normal custom of the world.

records.source: לְכָ֨ה נַשְׁקֶ֧ה אֶת־אָבִ֛ינוּ יַ֖יִן וְנִשְׁכְּבָ֣ה עִמּ֑וֹ וּנְחַיֶּ֥ה מֵאָבִ֖ינוּ זָֽרַע׃
records.gloss: Come, let us make drink our father wine, and let us lie with him, that we may keep alive from our father offspring.
pieces: Come, let us give our father wine to drink and then lie with him. That way we can keep our father's family line alive."

L.32: Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, so that we may preserve offspring through our father."

R.32: Let us get our father drunk with wine. Then we can sleep with him and have children by him. That way our father's family will not die out."

decisions.choice: to preserve offspring through our father: a plan born of despair
decisions.reason: Their aim is to keep the family line alive, but the means is incest, later forbidden in the law (Leviticus 18:6-7). The narrator tells the story plainly and without approval.

decisions.choice: offspring
decisions.reason: Literal uses "offspring" for zera, as elsewhere in Genesis.

records.source: וַתַּשְׁקֶ֧יןָ אֶת־אֲבִיהֶ֛ן יַ֖יִן בַּלַּ֣יְלָה ה֑וּא וַתָּבֹ֤א הַבְּכִירָה֙ וַתִּשְׁכַּ֣ב אֶת־אָבִ֔יהָ וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע בְּשִׁכְבָ֖הּ וּבְקׄוּמָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And they made drink their father wine on that night, and went in the firstborn and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down and when she arose.
pieces: That night they gave their father wine to drink, and the older daughter went in and slept with him. He was not aware of her lying down or getting up.

L.33: So they made their father drink wine that night, and the firstborn went in and lay with her father; and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

R.33: That night they gave their father a lot of wine. The older daughter went in and slept with him. He was so drunk that he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

decisions.choice: when she arose: the Hebrew text marks the word with dots
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts the word for "when she arose" carries special dots above it, one of a few places so marked. Their purpose is uncertain; ancient interpreters took them as raising a doubt, as if Lot did know when she rose. The word itself is not in doubt and is translated as written.

decisions.choice: He was so drunk that
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit that his not knowing was due to the wine.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הַבְּכִירָה֙ אֶל־הַצְּעִירָ֔ה הֵן־שָׁכַ֥בְתִּי אֶ֖מֶשׁ אֶת־אָבִ֑י נַשְׁקֶ֨נּוּ יַ֜יִן גַּם־הַלַּ֗יְלָה וּבֹ֨אִי֙ שִׁכְבִ֣י עִמּ֔וֹ וּנְחַיֶּ֥ה מֵאָבִ֖ינוּ זָֽרַע׃
records.gloss: And it was on the next day, and said the firstborn to the younger, here, I lay last night with my father; let us make him drink wine also tonight, and go in, lie with him, that we may keep alive from our father offspring.
pieces: The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "Last night I slept with my father. Let us give him wine to drink again tonight, and you go in and sleep with him. Then we will both keep our father's line alive."

L.34: And on the next day the firstborn said to the younger, "Look, I lay last night with my father. Let us make him drink wine tonight also; then you go in and lie with him, so that we may preserve offspring through our father."

R.34: The next day the older daughter said to her sister, "Last night I slept with our father. Let us get him drunk again tonight. Then you can go in and sleep with him. That way we can both have children by our father."

records.source: וַתַּשְׁקֶ֜יןָ גַּ֣ם בַּלַּ֧יְלָה הַה֛וּא אֶת־אֲבִיהֶ֖ן יָ֑יִן וַתָּ֤קָם הַצְּעִירָה֙ וַתִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמּ֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע בְּשִׁכְבָ֖הּ וּבְקֻמָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And they made drink also on that night their father wine, and arose the younger and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down and when she arose.
pieces: So again that night they gave their father wine, and the younger daughter went and slept with him. Again he was not aware of her lying down or getting up.

L.35: So that night also they made their father drink wine, and the younger arose and lay with him; and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

R.35: So that night they got their father drunk again, and the younger daughter slept with him. Again he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

records.source: וַֽתַּהֲרֶ֛יןָ שְׁתֵּ֥י בְנֽוֹת־ל֖וֹט מֵאֲבִיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And conceived [the] two daughters of Lot from their father.
pieces: In this way both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their own father.

L.36: Thus both the daughters of Lot became pregnant by their father.

R.36: So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.

records.source: וַתֵּ֤לֶד הַבְּכִירָה֙ בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ מוֹאָ֑ב ה֥וּא אֲבִֽי־מוֹאָ֖ב עַד־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And bore the firstborn a son and called his name Moab; he [is the] father of Moab until this day.
pieces: The older daughter had a son and named him Moab. He is the ancestor of the Moabites who live today.

L.37: And the firstborn bore a son and called his name Moab. He [is] the father of Moab to this day.

R.37: The older daughter had a son. She named him Moab. He is the ancestor of the Moabites, who are still a people today.

decisions.choice: Moab: heard as "from father"
decisions.reason: The name Moab sounds like "from father" (me'av), recalling how he was conceived. The Septuagint adds a sentence saying so. Moab became Israel's neighbor east of the Dead Sea (Numbers 22-25; Ruth 1).

decisions.choice: to this day: the narrator's own time
decisions.reason: The phrase links the story to readers who knew Moab as a people.

records.source: וְהַצְּעִירָ֤ה גַם־הִוא֙ יָ֣לְדָה בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֶּן־עַמִּ֑י ה֛וּא אֲבִ֥י בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן עַד־הַיּֽוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: And the younger, also she bore a son and called his name Ben-ammi; he [is the] father of [the] sons of Ammon until this day.
pieces: The younger daughter also had a son, and she named him Ben-ammi. He is the ancestor of the Ammonites who live today.

L.38: And the younger also bore a son and called his name Ben-ammi. He [is] the father of the sons of Ammon to this day.

R.38: The younger daughter also had a son. She named him Ben-ammi. He is the ancestor of the Ammonites, who are still a people today.

decisions.choice: Ben-ammi: "son of my kin"
decisions.reason: The name means "son of my people" or "son of my father's kin", again pointing to his origin. His descendants, "the sons of Ammon", lived east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 2:19).

decisions.choice: Moab and Ammon: Israel's relatives
decisions.reason: Israel was not to take land from Moab or Ammon, because they were Lot's descendants (Deuteronomy 2:9, 19). Ruth the Moabite became an ancestor of David (Ruth 4:13-17).
